QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_46

question.text: What are the gross open position limits for a Trading Member in USDINR currency futures and options?

answer.text: For a standard (non-bank) Trading Member, the limit is the higher of 15% of total open interest or USD 100 million; for a bank Trading Member authorized by RBI to deal in USDINR, the limit is the higher of 15% of total open interest or USD 1 billion
The Trading Member's limit is a uniform USD 50 million across all currency pairs, including USDINR
There is no Trading Member position limit — only the client-level limit is enforced
The Trading Member's limit is USD 100 million for proprietary positions only; client positions are excluded from the TM-level limit

explanation.text: The Logic: For USDINR, a Trading Member's gross open position across all contracts shall not exceed the higher of 15% of the total open interest of the market or USD 100 million. As a footnote exception, a bank Trading Member that is authorized by the RBI to deal in USDINR has a higher floor of USD 1 billion under the same higher-of rule. The Trap: USD 50 million is the figure for some non-INR cross-currency pairs at the TM level, not USDINR. The limit is the HIGHER of the two thresholds, not the lower. TM limits cover both client and proprietary positions of the TM. Note: The 15%-of-OI alternative ensures TM limits scale with market activity. The RBI-authorized bank-TM exception recognizes the larger scale at which authorized dealer banks operate in the USDINR market.
